document.title: Pakistan [Excised] On Afghanistan, HUA, Bin Laden
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] Reports former Ambassador Robert Oakley's non-official visit to Pakistan and his review of Afghanistan, including long-term dangers of Taliban success. Interlocutors discuss a possible Pushtoon nationalist/Islamic radical blowback, Harkat ul-Ansar (HUA) camps and fighters in Afghanistan with Taliban and UBL approval, and Pakistani leverage over the Taliban. ISI has advocated recognizing the Taliban and warded off Foreign Ministry attempts to close madrassas in the tribal agencies and near the border.

events.description: Oakley and Hoar, in Islamabad for a Track-II meeting, held private meetings with Pakistani officials about the Taliban, HUA and Bin Laden.
US Embassy Islamabad cable ISLAMA 1656 reports Oakley's memorandum and Pakistani concerns.

Taliban twice postponed a visit by U.S. Embassy personnel to HUA militant camps and had not agreed on a date.

key_claims: Pakistani interlocutors feared Taliban advances would push armed Tajiks, Uzbeks, Arabs and others into Central Asia and cause blowback into Pakistan.
Pakistani contacts expressed concern about HUA camps and fighters in Afghanistan with Taliban approval, and about Bin Laden.
Pakistan has leverage over the Taliban because nearly all their food and petroleum come via Pakistan; plans existed to restrict border crossings.
ISID reportedly supports hard-line Taliban from NWFP and Balochistan madrassas and refugee camps.
ISID advocated recognition of the Taliban while the MFA resisted, and ISID blocked MFA proposals to close border madrassas.
The Taliban twice postponed a US Embassy visit to militant camps and had not agreed a date.
